scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Office and Principle Room users (192.168.3.x, 192.168.4.x)
report they cannot reach Server Room (1.0.0.x) or Internet Lab
(128.168.0.x). IT Department and CS Department users say the
same. But Server Room ↔ Internet Lab works fine internally.
Find the broken link.

injection.action: shut down the WAN link to router1

pre_check.command: ip -br link show eth2 | grep -c UP

post_inject_check.command: ip -br link show eth2 | grep -c UP

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: router2 Serial2/0 (eth2), 20.20.0.0/8 link
Mechanism: router1 ↔ router2 over the 20.20.0.0/8 serial is
  the only path connecting routers 0/1's subnets to router2's
  Server Room + Internet Lab. With the link down, RIP on both
  sides ages out the unreachable prefixes and connectivity
  splits into two islands (router0+router1 side / router2 side).
Localization: router2 eth2 (or router1 eth3)
Root cause: WAN link router1<->router2 (20.20.0.0/8) is down
Fix: `ip link set eth2 up` on router2
scenario.fix_spec: `ip link set eth2 up` on router2

agent.diagnosis_text:
Affected component: the inter-router WAN link between the R1/R2 pair (wan_r1_r2), specifically router2’s uplink interface to that link.

Mechanism: With router2’s WAN interface down, the Server Room (1.0.0.0/8 on router2 eth0) and Internet Lab (128.168.0.0/16 on router2 eth1) remain reachable to each other locally on router2, but are isolated from the rest of the campus behind routers 0 and 1 (IT, CS, Office, Principle). Hosts in those departments cannot traverse to router2, so they cannot reach 1.0.0.x or 128.168.0.x.

Localization evidence:
- router2 ifconfig shows eth2 (wan_r1_r2) in DOWN state: flags=4098<BROADCAST,MULTICAST> state DOWN, inet 20.20.0.2/8.
- router1 ifconfig shows the opposite end (eth3) UP at 20.20.0.1/8.
- router1 routing table has RIP-learned routes to 1.0.0.0/8 and 128.168.0.0/16 via 20.20.0.2 dev eth3, but traffic will fail because router2’s interface is down.
- Server Room ↔ Internet Lab pings succeed (both on router2), while cross-department pings fail per user report and reachability snapshot.

Root cause: router2’s WAN interface eth2 (20.20.0.2/8) is down, breaking the wan_r1_r2 link.

Corrective fix: Bring up router2 eth2 and restore the physical/logical link to router1 eth3. Commands: ip link set eth2 up (or correct cabling). Verify IP 20.20.0.2/8, then ensure RIP is running on that interface so routes re-advertise. Confirm by pinging from Office/Principle/IT/CS to 1.0.0.x and 128.168.0.x afterward.

per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly names the R1–R2 WAN link (wan_r1_r2) and cites router2 eth2 at 20.20.0.2/8 (with router1 eth3 20.20.0.1/8) as down, matching the required affected link.

The report clearly separates the symptom (local Server Room/Internet Lab connectivity but failure from other departments) from the underlying split caused by the down R1–R2 WAN link, identifying the two isolated islands and root cause.
Recommends bringing router2's eth2 up (ip link set eth2 up) and restoring the link, which matches the expected fix.
